questions.title: Structural Sequence #1
questions.sequence: HH → HL → HH → HL → HH
questions.question: What market structure is developing in this sequence?
questions.explanation: Consecutive Higher Highs and Higher Lows define textbook bullish uptrend expansion.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #2
questions.sequence: LH → LL → LH → LL → LL
questions.question: What market structure is confirmed by consecutive lower extremes?
questions.explanation: Consecutive Lower Highs and Lower Lows confirm sellers are in full directional control.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #3
questions.sequence: Equal High → Equal Low → Equal High → Equal Low
questions.question: Price bounces between equal boundaries without higher or lower expansion. What is this?
questions.explanation: Equal highs and equal lows represent a balanced trading range.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #4
questions.sequence: HH → HL → HH → Failure to make HH → Break below HL
questions.question: After making Higher Highs, price prints a Lower High and breaks the previous Higher Low. What is this?

options.text: Break of Structure (BOS) from Bullish to Bearish

questions.explanation: Breaking below the most recent Higher Low marks a decisive structural shift.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #5
questions.sequence: LH → LL → LH → Higher Low → Break above LH
questions.question: In a downtrend, price prints a Higher Low followed by a break above the prior Lower High. What is this?

options.text: Change of Character (CHoCH) from Bearish to Bullish

questions.explanation: Breaking above the previous Lower High signals an initial bullish character change.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #6
questions.sequence: Resistance at 1.0850 → Spike to 1.0875 → Close at 1.0845
questions.question: A candle wicks 25 pips above resistance but closes back below it. What occurred?

options.text: Bull Trap / Liquidity Sweep above Resistance

questions.explanation: Spiking beyond a level and immediately closing inside creates a classic fakeout trap.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #7
questions.sequence: Support at 1.2500 → Break to 1.2440 → Pullback to 1.2498 → Rejection to 1.2400
questions.question: Broken support at 1.2500 is tested from below and rejects downward. What is this?
questions.explanation: Former support acting as new resistance upon retest is a verified S/R level flip.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #8
questions.sequence: Resistance at 150.00 → Break to 150.80 → Pullback to 150.05 → Bounce to 151.50
questions.question: Broken resistance at 150.00 is tested from above and bounces upward. What is this?
questions.explanation: Former resistance acting as new support upon retest is a confirmed level flip.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #9
questions.sequence: Equal High 1 → Equal High 2 → Equal High 3 → Sweep Wick → Collapse
questions.question: Triple tops are pierced by a single quick wick before an aggressive selloff. What happened?
questions.explanation: Equal highs accumulate buy stops that institutions target before initiating sell moves.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #10
questions.sequence: Equal Low 1 → Equal Low 2 → Equal Low 3 → Sweep Wick → Surge
questions.question: Triple bottoms are pierced by a sudden wick before a violent rally. What happened?
questions.explanation: Equal lows accumulate sell stops that are swept for liquidity before upward reversal.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #11
questions.sequence: Ascending Lows against Flat Resistance Ceiling
questions.question: Swing lows are steadily rising while swing highs hit the same flat resistance. What does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Ascending lows show buyers stepping in earlier on each dip, pressing against the resistance barrier.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #12
questions.sequence: Descending Highs against Flat Support Floor
questions.question: Swing highs are steadily falling while swing lows hit the same flat support floor. What does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Descending highs show sellers capping rallies earlier, pressing against the support floor.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #13
questions.sequence: HH1 → HL1 → HH2 (Extended Wick) → Deep Pullback → Equal Low
questions.question: A strong uptrend suddenly prints a deep retracement that touches the prior major swing low. What is happening?
questions.explanation: A deep pullback matching the previous low halts Higher Low progression and transitions into a range.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #14
questions.sequence: Wide Range → Range Squeeze → Volatility Compression
questions.question: Swing swings become smaller and volume drops toward a tight pivot. What phase is this?
questions.explanation: Compression represents market equilibrium where participants await catalysts for the next expansion.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #15
questions.sequence: Rising Trendline Touch 1 → Touch 2 → Touch 3 → Touch 4
questions.question: Price respects a diagonal floor connecting consecutive Higher Lows. What is this line called?
questions.explanation: An ascending trendline connects two or more rising Higher Lows, acting as diagonal support.

questions.title: Structural Sequence #16
questions.sequence: Falling Trendline Touch 1 → Touch 2 → Touch 3 → Touch 4
questions.question: Price respects a diagonal ceiling connecting consecutive Lower Highs. What is this line called?
questions.explanation: A descending trendline connects two or more declining Lower Highs, acting as diagonal resistance.
